$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

First, we create a matrix $Y$ containing all of the vertices of the larger recreational area:

$$
Y=[\begin{aligned}-15 & -15 & -21 \\ 4 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, if $X$ denotes the matrix that contains the corresponding vertices of the smaller recreational area, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}T\cdot X & =Y \\ T\cdot X & =[\begin{aligned}-15 & -15 & -21 \\ 4 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We need to reverse the action of the matrix $T.$ So, we multiply the above equation by ${T}^{-1},$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1}\cdot T\cdot X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-15 & -15 & -21 \\ 4 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}] \\ X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-15 & -15 & -21 \\ 4 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The inverse of $T$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{(-1)(-3)-0}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}X & ={T}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-15 & -15 & -21 \\ 4 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -2 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-15 & -15 & -21 \\ 4 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}15 & 15 & 21 \\ 18 & 24 & 24\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 & 7 \\ 6 & 8 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the vertices of the smaller recreational area are $L(5,6),$ $M(5,8),$ and $N(7,8).$
